database_metadata.name: Wazuh-to-MITRE ATT&CK Semantic Mapping Database
database_metadata.description: Event-level semantic mapping database translating Wazuh telemetry (alerts.json / archives.json) into MITRE ATT&CK techniques for adversary simulation labs. Purely declarative, correlation-free, and noise-restricted.

correlation_policy.note: All mappings are pure event-level semantic matches. No time windows, no sequence correlation, no stateful tracking.

confidence_score_rubric.0.85-0.95: Very strong signal (e.g., LSASS access, /etc/shadow read, web shell file creation)
confidence_score_rubric.0.70-0.84: Good signal but possible admin activity (e.g., sudo by non-admin, RDP from new IP)
confidence_score_rubric.0.50-0.69: Moderate signal, likely needs future correlation (e.g., whoami by service account)

lab_environment.siem_network: Ubuntu VM running Wazuh Manager + Zeek

noise_avoidance_rules: NO mappings for normal server maintenance: dpkg, apt, systemctl restart, normal cron from root, routine SSH admin logins.
Inherently noisy techniques (whoami, uname, ls) MUST be restricted to attacker IP 192.168.56.40, service accounts (www-data, tomcat, apache), or Wazuh suspicious rule groups.

Apache logs ONLY map attack patterns: SQL injection strings, scanner user-agents, suspicious HTTP methods, or paths like /manager/html, /wp-admin, /.env, ending in .jsp or .php when combined with POST.
Generic process creation (Event ID 4688, auditd EXECVE) is NOT mapped unless the command/executable is specifically tied to the technique.
correlation_required must ALWAYS be false. No time windows, no aggregations, no behavioral correlation.
confidence_score must reflect real discriminative power using the defined rubric.

semantic_conditions_subschema.conditions: Array of condition objects or nested logic blocks

condition_object.operator: One of the supported comparison operators
condition_object.value: string, number, boolean, or array (for 'in' operator)

semantic_conditions_subschema.nesting_rule: For OR logic inside an AND block, nest a sub-object with 'logic':'OR' and its own 'conditions' array.

mapping_structure.required_fields_rule: Must include every top-level field used in semantic_conditions.

schema_notes: All mappings are declarative, machine-readable, and SQL-free.
The semantic evaluator consumes semantic_conditions directly using dot-notation field access.
Field names preserve original Wazuh decoded_fields naming (decoder.name, data.audit.command, etc.).
Nested OR blocks are supported inside top-level AND logic for complex multi-signal matching.
confidence_score represents mapping discriminative strength, not runtime detection confidence.
related_techniques provides ATT&CK navigation links for multi-step attack chain analysis.
evidence_conditions are human-readable descriptions of what telemetry artifact indicates the technique.
false_positive_notes document legitimate activity that could trigger the mapping and how to triage.

semantic_match.description: Evaluates a single decoded event against a mapping's semantic_conditions tree.
semantic_match.logic: Recursive tree evaluation. Each node is either a condition leaf (field, operator, value) or a logic node (logic, conditions[]).

field_resolver.null_handling: If any segment in the path is missing, the field is treated as null and the condition evaluates to False.

operator_evaluator.description: Applies the operator between the resolved field value and the condition value.

operator_matrix.in: Field value is a member of the provided array
operator_matrix.not_in: Field value is NOT a member of the provided array
operator_matrix.contains: Substring match (case-sensitive or case-insensitive depending on engine config)

required_fields_guard.description: Pre-evaluation filter. If any path in required_fields is absent from decoded_fields, the mapping is skipped entirely.
required_fields_guard.purpose: Avoids null-reference errors and short-circuits irrelevant mappings.

confidence_scorer.description: Returns the static confidence_score from the mapping metadata. Not dynamically computed at runtime.
confidence_scorer.use_case: Downstream prioritization and alert severity tuning.

evidence_conditions: Apache access log shows known vulnerability scanner User-Agent
Raw log contains masscan reference indicating port scanning activity
mappings.false_positive_notes: Legitimate security audits may use similar tools. Restrict to attacker subnet 192.168.56.0/24 or validate against authorized scanning windows.
mappings.explanation: Scanner user-agents like Nikto, SQLMap, Nessus, or OpenVAS in Apache logs indicate automated vulnerability scanning against the lab web server.

evidence_conditions: HTTP status 403 or 500 combined with SQL injection patterns in URL
Access to Tomcat manager or path traversal attempts observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Application errors may produce 500 status codes legitimately. The presence of SQLi strings or manager paths confirms malicious intent.
mappings.explanation: SQL injection payloads, path traversal, or brute-force attempts against Tomcat manager indicate exploitation of public-facing applications.

evidence_conditions: Syscheck detects new .jsp, .php, or .war files in web application directories
Apache POST requests to known web shell filenames
mappings.false_positive_notes: Developers may legitimately deploy .war files or .php scripts. Context of vulnerability exploitation preceding the file creation confirms malicious web shell.
mappings.explanation: Web shells uploaded to Tomcat or Apache directories provide persistent remote access and are commonly placed via exploited manager interfaces.

evidence_conditions: PowerShell executed with encoded command flag -enc
Execution policy bypass or known malicious cmdlets like Invoke-Mimikatz observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: System administrators use PowerShell legitimately. Encoded commands, bypass flags, and credential dumping cmdlets are high-confidence malicious indicators.
mappings.explanation: PowerShell with encoded commands, execution policy bypass, or known malicious cmdlets is a primary execution vector in Windows post-exploitation.

evidence_conditions: Windows Event Channel shows execution of cmd.exe
Wscript.exe, cscript.exe, or mshta.exe execution observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Batch files and scripts run legitimately in enterprise environments. Context of lateral movement or credential compromise confirms malicious use.
mappings.explanation: Non-PowerShell Windows scripting interpreters like cmd.exe, wscript, cscript, and mshta are commonly used by attackers for execution and payload delivery.

evidence_conditions: Multiple SSH authentication failures from single source
Windows Event ID 4625 indicates failed logon attempt
mappings.false_positive_notes: Users with forgotten passwords may trigger SSH failures. Windows 4625 events may occur during normal operations. Focus on attacker subnet.
mappings.explanation: Repeated failed authentication attempts against SSH or Windows SMB indicate brute force password guessing in the lab environment.

evidence_conditions: SSH authentication failures containing invalid user string
Same password attempted across multiple non-existent or valid usernames
mappings.false_positive_notes: Legitimate users with typos may trigger invalid user messages. Volume and pattern distinguish spraying from isolated mistakes.
mappings.explanation: SSH failures with invalid user indicate the attacker is spraying a common password across multiple usernames against the Ubuntu server.

evidence_conditions: Windows Event Channel shows LSASS process access
Mimikatz, sekurlsa, or procdump execution observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Some security tools legitimately access LSASS. The presence of Mimikatz or procdump targeting LSASS is definitive malicious activity.
mappings.explanation: Access to LSASS memory or execution of Mimikatz/procdump on the Windows AD server indicates credential dumping activity.

evidence_conditions: Auditd log shows read access to /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd
Command executed by non-system user or attacker IP
mappings.false_positive_notes: System administrators may legitimately view these files. Restrict to attacker IP or service accounts to reduce noise.
mappings.explanation: Reading /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd is a direct indicator of credential dumping on Linux systems, commonly performed after initial access.

evidence_conditions: Windows Event ID 5140 indicates network share access
References to psexec, ADMIN$, or C$ admin shares observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Legitimate administrative tools may access admin shares. psexec usage or ADMIN$ access from non-admin systems is suspicious.
mappings.explanation: SMB admin share access or psexec usage indicates lateral movement via Windows administrative shares in the lab domain.

evidence_conditions: Linux wget or curl downloads script or executable files
Windows certutil, bitsadmin, or Invoke-WebRequest observed
mappings.false_positive_notes: System updates and legitimate downloads may use these tools. The target file extensions and suspicious destinations confirm tool transfer.
mappings.explanation: Downloading scripts or executables via wget, curl, certutil, or bitsadmin indicates attackers are staging tools on compromised hosts.

evidence_conditions: Base64 encoded commands in Linux auditd logs
PowerShell -enc, FromBase64String, or bxor obfuscation in Windows events
mappings.false_positive_notes: Base64 is used legitimately in many contexts. Combined with suspicious command structure or execution context confirms evasion intent.
mappings.explanation: Base64 encoding and PowerShell obfuscation are common defense evasion techniques used to hide malicious command content from detection.

evidence_conditions: Execution from /tmp directory on Linux via bash or sh
Execution from C:\Users or Windows Temp directories
mappings.false_positive_notes: Applications and installers may legitimately run from temp directories. Correlation with prior exploitation or unknown file hashes confirms malicious execution.
mappings.explanation: Payload execution from temporary or public directories is a common post-exploitation pattern for running staged malicious files.

attack_technique.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys

evidence_conditions: Registry modifications to Run or RunOnce keys
Changes under CurrentVersion or HKEY_CURRENT_USER hives
mappings.false_positive_notes: Software installers may legitimately add run keys. Unauthorized modifications outside of change management indicate persistence.
mappings.explanation: Modifications to Windows Run or RunOnce registry keys establish persistence by executing malicious code on user logon or system boot.

evidence_conditions: Auditd shows crontab or cron command execution
Syscheck detects new files in /etc/cron.d
mappings.false_positive_notes: System maintenance and legitimate applications use cron. Unauthorized cron entries or modifications by non-admin users indicate persistence.
mappings.explanation: Cron job creation or modification on the Ubuntu server establishes scheduled execution for maintaining attacker access.

attack_technique.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

evidence_conditions: Windows Event ID 7045 or 4697 indicates new service creation
Command line shows sc create or service registration
mappings.false_positive_notes: Software installations legitimately create services. Services created outside of authorized deployment tools or with suspicious binary paths are malicious.
mappings.explanation: Creation of a new Windows service establishes persistence by ensuring malicious payload execution on system startup.

evidence_conditions: net user /domain command execution observed
dsquery user or Get-ADUser cmdlets executed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may query domain users legitimately. Execution from compromised accounts or outside of normal admin activity is suspicious.
mappings.explanation: Domain account discovery via net user, dsquery, or PowerShell cmdlets indicates reconnaissance after compromising the Windows AD server.

evidence_conditions: net group /domain command execution observed
dsquery group or Get-ADGroup cmdlets executed
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may query domain groups legitimately. Execution from compromised accounts or unexpected hosts is suspicious.
mappings.explanation: Domain group discovery via net group, dsquery, or PowerShell cmdlets indicates reconnaissance to identify privileged groups for targeting.

evidence_conditions: Sudo session opened for root user
Rule 5402 fires on successful sudo to ROOT
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators legitimately use sudo. Execution from compromised accounts or unusual commands indicates privilege escalation.
mappings.explanation: Successful sudo to root establishes elevated privileges on the target system, representing a privilege escalation step in the attack chain.

evidence_conditions: ping, traceroute, or tracepath executed via auditd
Source IP is the attacker Kali VM
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators use ping and traceroute for troubleshooting. Restricting to the attacker IP eliminates legitimate network diagnostics.
mappings.explanation: Network discovery commands from the attacker IP indicate active reconnaissance to identify live hosts within the lab subnet.

mappings.evidence_conditions: SSH connection from attacker IP followed by whoami execution in the resulting session.
mappings.false_positive_notes: whoami is commonly used by administrators. Restrict the source SSH event to the known attacker IP.
mappings.explanation: Correlates an SSH connection from the attacker with subsequent whoami execution.

evidence_conditions: Successful SSH authentication from attacker IP after brute force
Windows Event ID 4624 with Logon Type 10 indicating remote interactive logon
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may legitimately RDP or SSH from the same subnet. Validate against known admin workstations and time-of-day patterns.
mappings.explanation: Successful authentication from the attacker IP following brute force indicates compromised valid credentials are being used for access.

evidence_conditions: A sudo execution occurs after a successful SSH connection from the lab attacker IP 192.168.56.40.

source_event.description: Successful SSH authentication from the known attacker IP

mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may legitimately use sudo after SSH login. The correlation is restricted to the known attacker IP in the lab environment.
mappings.explanation: Sudo execution is considered a privilege-escalation signal when it follows an SSH authentication originating from the known attacker machine.

evidence_conditions: Windows Event ID 4624 with Logon Type 10
Source IP matches attacker Kali VM
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may legitimately RDP into servers. The attacker IP 192.168.56.40 is not a known admin workstation in this lab.
mappings.explanation: RDP logon events from the attacker IP indicate lateral movement to the Windows AD server after credential compromise.

evidence_conditions: Successful SSH authentication from attacker IP
Follows brute force pattern against Ubuntu server
mappings.false_positive_notes: Administrators may SSH from the lab subnet. The attacker IP 192.168.56.40 is the Kali VM and not an authorized admin host.
mappings.explanation: Successful SSH from the attacker IP after brute force indicates lateral movement and persistent access to the Ubuntu web server.

evidence_conditions: The whoami command is executed after a successful SSH connection from the known attacker IP 192.168.56.40.

source_event.description: Successful SSH authentication from the known attacker IP

mappings.false_positive_notes: whoami is commonly executed by administrators and service processes. It should not map independently. Restricting it to a recent SSH success from 192.168.56.40 significantly reduces false positives.
mappings.explanation: whoami is treated as suspicious only when it follows a successful SSH connection from the known attacker machine.
